notes: These evals test the PLAN behavior after per-project preferences were removed. Preferences resolve from defaults overlaid by ~/.muggle-ai/preferences.json only; muggle-local-preferences-set rejects a `scope` argument. The prompts ask for a step-by-step plan rather than execution, since writing preferences mutates the user's home directory. Assertions check that the plan never offers a per-project scope, never passes `scope`, and confirms before applying a setting the user framed as project-specific.

evals.prompt: For this repo only, I want the Electron browser to actually show up when tests run — it's a UI-heavy project and I like watching it. Leave my other projects alone. Walk me through what you'd do.

assertions.name: states_preferences_are_user_level
assertions.text: Plan states that preferences are user-level and apply to every repo, so a per-repo setting is not supported.

assertions.name: does_not_offer_project_scope
assertions.text: Plan does NOT offer a 'this project only' option, and does not claim a project-scoped preferences file can be written.

assertions.name: no_scope_argument
assertions.text: Plan does not pass a `scope` argument to muggle-local-preferences-set; it calls the tool with key and value only.

assertions.name: confirms_before_global_write
assertions.text: Plan explicitly confirms with the user before writing, because the user asked for one repo and the write will affect all of them.

assertions.name: names_the_correct_key
assertions.text: Plan identifies showElectronBrowser as the key to set.

assertions.name: does_not_invent_a_workaround
assertions.text: Plan does not invent a per-repo mechanism (env var, local override file, wrapper script) to simulate project scope.

evals.prompt: show me my muggle settings and where they're stored

assertions.name: resolution_is_two_layer
assertions.text: Plan describes resolution as defaults overlaid by ~/.muggle-ai/preferences.json, with no third per-project layer.

assertions.name: names_the_global_path
assertions.text: Plan names ~/.muggle-ai/preferences.json as the storage location.

assertions.name: no_project_file_mentioned
assertions.text: Plan does not tell the user that a preferences file inside the repo is read or honoured.

assertions.name: reads_from_session_context_or_tool
assertions.text: Plan reads current values from the session-context preferences line or the preferences tool rather than guessing.

evals.prompt: I've got a .muggle-ai/preferences.json checked into my repo with autoLogin set to never, but muggle keeps logging me in automatically. Why isn't it being picked up?

assertions.name: explains_file_is_not_read
assertions.text: Plan explains that a preferences file inside the project is no longer read — preferences are user-level.

assertions.name: points_at_global_file
assertions.text: Plan points the user at ~/.muggle-ai/preferences.json as the file that actually takes effect.

assertions.name: offers_to_reapply_globally
assertions.text: Plan offers to re-apply the affected key globally, noting it will then apply to every repo.

assertions.name: does_not_delete_user_file
assertions.text: Plan does not delete or rewrite the user's in-repo preferences file without asking.

assertions.name: no_scope_argument
assertions.text: Plan does not attempt to pass a `scope` argument to make the project file work.
